# freight-audit-lab

By [Shreyansh Agrawal](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shreyansh2003/) · [Code](https://github.com/shreyansh2003/freight-audit-lab) · Live dashboard: [dashboard link] · Synthetic data; every dollar figure is an estimate.

A simulated freight invoice audit and month-end accrual pipeline. It generates 10,000 shipments and 10,388 invoices from 8 invented carriers, seeds them with billing errors and traps (invoices that look wrong but are not), audits them, and accrues unbilled freight.

## The comparison

The baseline is built to lack business context, so the question is which context matters and how much, not whether spreadsheets are bad. It has the engine's rules, tolerances and fuel check and strips BOL formatting, but lacks effective dates, reweigh certificates, authorization timing, and which invoices a rebill replaced.

| | Precision | Recall | False flags |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Engine | 99.9% | 89.7% | 1 |
| Baseline | 41.9% | 89.5% | 1,552 |

Recall is nearly the same; precision is not. A false flag is a dispute the carrier rejects. Its 1,552 false flags each have one cause: rate amendments 554, late authorizations 353, reweigh certificates 207, rebills and balance dues 200, weight errors re-flagged as rate errors 155, BOL typos or dropped zeros 69, other 14. Missing context, not string cleaning.

## Read the engine's numbers with care

Near-perfect engine precision is expected: I built the generator and the engine, so it knows the world it is tested on. It shows coherent logic, not survival on real invoices. Four results:

1. **Where the baseline fails.** Its duplicate flags were 60% wrong (200 of 334), 100% of the wrong ones from rebills and balance-due invoices.
2. **Where the engine misses.** It missed 129 injected errors, 118 of them below its own tolerances, worth $691 (answer-key dollars). No tolerance change clears the $1,000 materiality bar (an estimate; best gain $182), so all 4 stay.
3. **The systemic-issue test.** Carrier F Trucking was flagged on 178 of 182 fuel surcharges shipped Aug 2025 to Oct 2025, against 1.5% at the other truckload carriers (p < 1e-300). Each overcharge is only about $44 (estimate): the pattern is the finding. The test also flagged 1 weaker pattern (a high-error carrier): triage, not proof.
4. **The accrual diagnosis.** Linehaul and fuel accrual accuracy is close to exact by construction: generator, audit and accruals all price from `contract.py`. Accruals landed 0.24% below eventual payable (mean monthly error 0.31%, estimates), but months net over- and under-accruals; per shipment the mean error is 5.6%, and 17% of shipment-months miss by over 10%. Accessorials were 1.6% of accrued dollars but 61% of the net shortfall, and 43% of it is late-recorded authorizations (set by the injected late rate).

## Approach

Generator with traps, four carrier layouts, normalization and matching, re-rating, rules, scoring against a sealed answer key, month-end accruals. The answer key is sealed from audit and accrual code (a test enforces it); an accrual at M uses only what was known at M.

## Limitations

- Synthetic data with injected error rates, so the recoverable estimate ($294,344, 2.45% of billed) is circular, not a finding.
- Invented formats; no undercharges, in-transit accruals or scale noise (so no weight-tolerance calibration).
- The engine's 1 false flag is a typo'd BOL that matched no shipment; left in.

## With real data I would

Ingest EDI 210 and PDF invoices, calibrate tolerances on dispute outcomes, use carrier fuel tables, and add undercharges.

## Run it

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m freight_audit_lab.run
streamlit run streamlit_app.py
```

Repo map: `freight_audit_lab/` (pipeline), `config.yaml` (every tunable), `data/`, `outputs/`, `tests/`. See `ASSUMPTIONS.md`, `WALKTHROUGH.md` and `SPEC.md`.
